assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only three-days-of-happiness:kusunoki@original-novel#novel-monograph (the canonical v1.0 Kusunoki novel monograph, qualified COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY, accepted with corrections and passed on receiving review against the Japanese EPUB) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the single Japanese witness TDH-JP-01, native chapters 1-15, end paratext excluded. The row's U01 and U02 readings are curated evidence on this subject but were not relied on and are not cited. The fifteen readings, the longitudinal notebook, the novel synthesis, the completion audit, the release-decision record and the Miyagi, Himeno, Shinbashi and substitute-watcher monographs are not cited, and nothing is borrowed from them. The audit's reconstruction-readiness table, its RETROSPECTIVE_CONSISTENCY_TEST caution and the project's statement that no reconstruction operation is authorized were read as method inputs, not conclusions. No translation, adaptation or other edition is assessed, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: From the recounted childhood (about age four, Ch09 P0141; age ten in Ch01) through the first of his last three days (Ch15 P0127), with the story present running from the sale day at twenty (Ch02) through about day 57 (the second sale, Ch14 P0155-P0196) and the next day (Ch15). States are split at the sale (Ch02 P0179-P0186), the station night (Ch08 P0007-P0091), Himeno's letter and the resolve to expect nothing (Ch10 P0190-P0259), Miyagi's confession and the debt goal (Ch12 P0136-P0215), the resolve to live foolishly (Ch13 P0090), the second sale (Ch14 P0155-P0168) and Miyagi's return (Ch15 P0053-P0100). Day counts are the monograph's approximate inferences. Nothing after Ch15 P0127, including the remaining shared days and his death, is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph builds an account of Kusunoki, the narrator, around worth: a chain of located self-valuations from the boy's three billion yen (Ch01 P0028) through the appraisal (Ch02 P0158-P0172), the thirty-yen revelation (Ch12 P0164-P0167) and the refusal of eternity (Ch14 P0168) to the closing valuation (Ch15 P0124-P0127). Around it are kindness read as role-bound, a childhood frame he names himself (Ch11 P0131-P0133; Ch10 P0256); passive "devil's-proof" hope (Ch05 P0070-P0073); authenticity against staged performance; and protection by concealment and unilateral action (section 5.5). The conditional profile (section 13) gives triggers and counterconditions and predicts his mistakes: credulity before confident verdicts, escalating certainty from weak premises (Ch11 P0142-P0148), the thrown glass, and the aborted assault. Not A: the motives of the first sale and of his ten-year fidelity to Himeno, his childhood rival, stay open among named rivals (TDH-C009, TDH-C003), and his self-reports are locally contradicted by his own narration (section 2.4). Not C: the account says which condition changes his response (a protected hope threatened, mockery of a valued thing, kindness with or without its own reasons, a chance to act for someone he loves) and locates each.

Eight phases for Kusunoki, from the deflation of the sale day to the reunion, are each given what changed, for whom and the stated cause, and the monograph separates development from late disclosure of older traits (the attraction dated to the first meeting, Ch06 P0007; the painting history, Ch14 P0179-P0188; the bedtime habit, Ch10 P0236). The record's own chronology is handled: most of chapters 1-11 were first written about day 30 (Ch12 P0052-P0074; TDH-C010). Counterevidence: the record's revision points are unknown, and the closing changes are self-report hedged with 多分. Not A: day counts are inferences and the identity of the printed text with his notebook is itself an inference. Not C: states are located and causally ordered with an explicit change table.

The written Japanese voice of Kusunoki is documented: 俺 throughout, 僕 only in the boy's letter (Ch09 P0031-P0035); a register table by interlocutor, polite to elders, shopkeepers and service roles, plain to peers, rivals and to Miyagi, the shop clerk who becomes his watcher, from Ch03 even when they are polite to him (Shinbashi); あんた to Miyagi from Ch03 P0106 to Ch12 P0177 and her name only from Ch13, from a search of his quoted speech; and narrating habits (correction from choice to incapacity, stacked hedges, denied motives, aphorism, 26 sesame-dot emphases with none in Ch15). Counterevidence: a printed novel has no performed voice, and his speech reaches the page only as he chose to quote it, some of it unbracketed. Not A: no frequency lexicon beyond targeted searches and no spoken performance. Not C: register is located across interlocutors and phases with negative constraints (no direct spoken avowal of love to Miyagi).

Ordinary life is among the densest parts of the monograph on Kusunoki: money and its rationing, cider bookending the story (Ch02 P0091-P0092; Ch15 P0007), cigarettes, vending machines (Ch11 P0049-P0077), the second-hand Cub, used books and CDs, walking and fasting to think, light sleep, dress, aversions, and a table separating stable preferences from situational choices. Not A: it covers a poor student's summer at twenty under a death sentence, and ordinary life before the sale is shown only in summary. Not C: the preferences recur across contexts with located anchors and an explicit stable-versus-situational account.

Directional sections condition Kusunoki's conduct by partner and phase. Toward Miyagi: from clerk (instant trust, disowned at Ch02 P0147) through watcher, the station night, companion, intimacy and the foolish summer to the return, with a directional trust, disclosure, initiative, dependency and protection table. Toward Himeno: rival and only interlocutor at ten, an imagined audience for ten years, one evening and her letter. Toward shopkeepers and elders: a reticent, polite regular who protects them from his troubles. Toward peers: Naruse, Wakana and the hostile acquaintance. Toward the town: from target to known figure. Counterevidence: every other side is his reading or their testimony; family is thin and testimony only (section 8.3). Not A: the family and adult-Himeno relations are thin. Not C: partner-specific conduct and register are located and contrasted.

Kusunoki's interior is richly self-reported, and the monograph tests self-report against what the narration shows (section 2.4) and separates the boy, the experiencing twenty-year-old and the writer (section 2.1). His own words give deciding reasons for most choices: the wish to leave (Ch02 P0183-P0184), the hope that keeps him from selling down (Ch05 P0070-P0073), the debt goal (Ch12 P0210-P0215), the refusal of eternity (Ch14 P0168). Counterevidence: the decisive moments are often elided and explained afterwards, and the narrating self has a later vantage than the experiencing self. Not A: interior access is self-report whose revision points are unknown. Not C: interior states are located and checked against conduct.

Kusunoki's conflict pattern is stated and located: retort (Ch03 P0120), silent reproach (Ch06 P0080-P0084), displaced explosion (the glass, Ch06 P0094), then flight or self-punishment (Ch06 P0097-P0098; Ch07 P0088); restraint by Ch07 P0084; late non-retaliation (Ch14 P0008). Against another's wishes about his own life he acts alone and explains later (Miyagi's warning about Himeno, her request to forget the debt, her plea to stay; section 5.5). Counterevidence: the cause of the station stop is narrated as affective, with unnarrated fear of death and exhaustion as rivals (U08 section 4.4), and that stop is a single case. Not A: that single case. Not C: an ordered, phase-conditioned pattern across many scenes.

The monograph gives Kusunoki's stated reasons at located ethically weighted choices: the licence a dying man claims for reading every capsule letter (Ch07 P0073); means for repaying Miyagi's debt weighed and crime rejected because she would not want it (Ch13 P0006-P0031); silence so the old bookseller will not feel responsible (Ch13 P0037); and the inference that he protects by concealment and acts for others without consent. The gravest act, the station impulse, is licensed by list item 3 and the arithmetic of his death (Ch08 P0009), and its stop is narrated as imagination and borrowed sadness, not reasoning (section 10). Not B: no discriminating account of how he weighs harm against licence beyond that single stop, which the profile rates weak to moderate. Not D: the reasons are located and a conditional rule is stated.

Kusunoki's humor is described by kind and function (section 7.5): deadpan wit under pressure (Ch02 P0034), self-deprecating jokes about his worth that give the first shared joke with Miyagi (Ch08 P0085-P0086) and his response to the thirty yen (Ch12 P0167), argument by hypothetical, courtship under cover of a joke (Ch10 P0059-P0065), and late play (Ch13 P0130-P0133; Ch14 P0102). The profile uses the joke as a deflection when he is asked for a feeling. Not A: his humor is known only as he chose to record it. Not C: forms are located across phases and tied to what they do.

The novel is a complete standalone work, and the monograph covers Kusunoki across all fifteen native chapters, with locators to the witness and routes to readings and notebook IDs (section 15). It passed self-containment and, after corrections, fidelity review, and its revised portrait passed receiving review against the Japanese EPUB, according to the discovery row. Not A: it is one derived synthesis whose locators resolve to readings and a notebook outside the cited set, and the project describes its receiving reviews as bounded rather than exhaustive. Not C: coverage is whole-work and routed to stable claim and state IDs.

The evidence affirmatively bounds Kusunoki: he never avows love to Miyagi in direct speech (Ch14 P0080 and Ch15 P0100 name it only in narration); he does not apologize in words after the station night; he never contacts Himeno after her letter (Ch10 P0208-P0215); his family never learns of the sale; contradictions are listed rather than resolved (the painting history, Ch10 P0119 against Ch14 P0182-P0188); and abstention zones are explicit. Not A: several bounds are absences of narration rather than located contradictions. Not C: the limitation tests are located against opportunities the text gave.

A chronology table locates Kusunoki's states by age and approximate day, from about four to the first of his last three days, and the phases are anchored to chapter and paragraph. Not A: the story-present days are inferences, and when the record's passages, including Ch15, were written or revised is unstated. Not C: the sequence is explicit and split at located state changes.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation: 俺 in all present-day speech; polite です/ます to elders, shopkeepers and service figures (the old bookseller, the old woman, the photo-shop owner, the appraiser); plain speech and あんた to peers, rivals and men met as equals even when they are polite to him (Shinbashi).
Toward Miyagi: plain speech from Ch03; あんた before Ch13 and her name without a second-person pronoun from Ch13; no keigo to her after the shop.
No direct spoken avowal of love to Miyagi; asked for a feeling he deflects into a joke, acts, or thanks her.
A phase must be selected; no acoustic performance, and no line after Ch15 P0127.
scenario_readiness.note: Located register, address and negative constraints support short illustrative lines for Kusunoki toward sampled interlocutors at a selected phase; the printed medium and his selective quotation keep the use narrow.

conditions: Predictions use only the profile's mechanisms (section 13): acceptance of confident verdicts with an exception for a protected hope; indirect approach and face-saving retreat when lonely; withdrawal of goodwill when a valued thing is mocked; suspicion of role-bound kindness until reasons are given; a tendency toward solitary, concealed action for someone he loves that can override that person's expressed wish (section 5.5), held as a tendency, not a required step, with the choice in a new case left open; politeness to elders and plainness to equals.
His mistakes are predicted as well as his care: credulity, over-confident inference chains, displaced outbursts early, and the capability shown at the station night.
Where the evidence holds motives open (why he sold, why he kept faith with Himeno, why he stopped at the station), the rivals are presented, not resolved.
The words of a declaration of feeling are not predicted.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One selected phase of the story present from the sale day (Ch02) to the reunion (Ch15 P0053-P0127): deflation (Ch02), days 1-3 (Ch03-Ch07), the station night (Ch08), the Himeno test (Ch09-Ch10, before or after her letter at Ch10 P0190), companionship (Ch11), revelation (Ch12, before or after the confession), the foolish summer (Ch13-Ch14, before or after the second sale) or the last day (Ch15). Childhood is used only as recounted history.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Miyagi in the relationship state of the selected phase; elders and shopkeepers of the kind sampled (the old bookseller, the CD clerk, the old woman); peers and opponents of the kind sampled (Naruse, Wakana, the substitute watcher, Shinbashi, the hostile acquaintance); townspeople and strangers in the late phase. His parents, his brother and an adult Himeno after her letter are excluded.
setting_constraints: The novel's world and its supernatural economy of lifespan, time and health, with Kusunoki under a sentence of months or days.
The town, his home town and places of the kinds shown; no Kusunoki with an open future.
No sexual conduct beyond what is narrated and nothing after Ch15 P0127.

scenario_readiness.note: The conditional profile supports bounded extrapolation for Kusunoki inside the novel's world at a selected phase of the three months. It does not support a Kusunoki with a future.

conditions: Habits and tastes from the stable column of the monograph's preference table (cider and canned drinks, cigarettes, vending machines, used books and CDs, the Cub, walking, light sleep).
Early phases are avoidant and self-conscious before observers; from about Ch13 he is openly, publicly foolish with Miyagi; the phase must be selected.
Money follows the narrated situation of the selected phase (poverty before the sale, the giving away at Ch10, the last war chest at Ch11, ¥187 at Ch15).
scenario_readiness.note: Dense, recurring ordinary-life evidence and located conduct with shopkeepers and strangers support bounded everyday scenes for Kusunoki, phase-specific in openness.

conditions: Only the located mechanisms: the dying man's licence for small transgressions; weighing means for someone he loves by what that person would want, as narrated for the debt goal (Ch13 P0006-P0031); a separate tendency toward solitary, concealed action that can override an expressed wish, as in the second sale against Miyagi's plea (Ch14 P0142), whose deliberation is not narrated and is not reconstructed as that weighing; protecting others from responsibility by silence.
The station stop is one case narrated as imagination of harm and her sadness, with fear of death and exhaustion as unnarrated rivals; it is not generalized into a rule that he always stops.
No ethical stance outside the novel's world or after Ch15 P0127.
scenario_readiness.note: Located reasons and one conditional rule support narrow extrapolation of Kusunoki's choices; general moral reasoning in a new situation is not supported.

conditions: Toward Miyagi only in the selected phase: attraction concealed early (Ch06 P0007-P0010), the station night unsoftened, hesitant self-checked approaches in the companion phase, open intimacy after her confession, the wish to be remembered and then to be forgotten for her sake.
Toward Himeno only at the narrated points (age ten, the dinner, the aftermath of her letter); no further meeting is generated.
No sexual conduct beyond kisses, embraces and a shared futon, and no spoken declaration of love.
scenario_readiness.note: The relationship with Miyagi is the most documented part of the novel and is phase-located; the Himeno relation is located at its narrated points.

Work appears only in passing for Kusunoki: the beer-garden collapse (Ch02 P0004), casual labour when money runs low (Ch13 P0101) and a university he stops attending under his list. The evidence does not sample working conduct enough to extrapolate it.

known_limits.statement: Everything about Kusunoki comes through his own record. His self-reports are often local and contradicted by what his narration shows, and every other character's feelings reach the page as his readings or as their testimony; a model must keep those apart.

Kusunoki's motives for the first sale (habituation and a wish to exit against despair, impatience and face-saving, TDH-C009), for his fidelity to Himeno (TDH-C003) and for the station stop are held open among named rivals, and whether the debt goal was revived or never set aside before the second sale is undecided (TDH-C061).
Kusunoki's late openness, gratitude and public foolishness are bound to a man with weeks to live and to one companion; the evidence gives no basis for projecting them onto a Kusunoki with a future.
The novel narrates the first morning and the reunion of Kusunoki's last three days and only projects the rest; the remaining shared days and his death are outside the evidence.

The printed text is identified with Kusunoki's notebook only by strong inference, with a later redaction as a recorded rival; most of chapters 1-11 were first written about day 30, and which passages were revised later, and when chapter 15 was written, are unknown (TDH-C010).
Kusunoki's voice is written register in a printed novel; no performed voice, intonation or accent is available, and some of his speech is reported without brackets or not remembered.
Kusunoki's parents and brother are known only through his account, never shown in person, and his conduct toward them in person is an abstention zone.

What Kusunoki believes about the shop's rules, his forfeited future and Miyagi's feelings rests on testimony, much of it later admitted by Miyagi to be lies (Ch12 P0193); his acceptance of a claim is not evidence that it is true.
The cited evidence contains no reconstruction model, probe or held-out evaluation of Kusunoki; the monograph's conditional profile is a literary reading aid it states has not been tested.
